headline: GOLD NEAR $3,544 AS DECEMBER FED HIKE PROBABILITY HITS 96.4% — October PCE Due Today; Last Data Before Dec. 8-9 FOMC
snippet: Spot gold is trading near $3,544 per ounce on November 25 as CME FedWatch puts the probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the December 8-9 Federal Reserve meeting at 96.4%, with a 3.6% tail risk of a larger 50-basis-point move. The October Personal Consumption Expenditures price index — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge — is due today and represents the last major data release before the FOMC decision; a soft print could be the catalyst for gold's first credible technical recovery since late October, while an upside surprise risks extending the November rout past the $3,500 floor.

headline: SUN SILVER DRILLS 55.8m AT 72 G/T AgEq ABOVE ITS OWN RESOURCE — MV0009 Finds Silver 42m Above 539Moz Maverick Deposit, Nevada
snippet: Sun Silver (ASX: SS1) reported that drill hole MV0009 at its Maverick project in Nevada returned 55.8 metres at 72 grams per tonne silver equivalent — with the entire interval positioned approximately 42 metres above the top of the company's existing 539 million ounce silver resource. Finding oxide-zone mineralisation above and outside the current resource boundary suggests the system is shallower and more expansive than the deposit model currently reflects, a classic setup for resource expansion in the next drill campaign and a development economics improvement at a time when silver is under rate-hike pressure.

headline: BHP UNVEILS $17.4B PLAN TO DOUBLE SOUTH AUSTRALIA COPPER OUTPUT BY 2040 — Phase One IRR 14-17%; FID Due H1 2027
snippet: BHP unveiled a plan on November 23 to invest between $13.6 billion and $17.4 billion to double its South Australian copper output to approximately 500,000 tonnes per year by 2035, with a final investment decision due in H1 2027 and a targeted IRR of 14-17% at current copper prices. The expansion spans Olympic Dam, Carrapateena, Prominent Hill and Ankata — collectively the largest undeveloped copper region in a AAA-jurisdiction — and positions BHP as the primary supply-side beneficiary of the AI-driven copper demand thesis that pushed the metal from US$9,000 to US$14,694 per tonne before November's AI selloff. For junior copper explorers in South Australia, BHP committing a capital allocation of this scale to the region is the strongest possible endorsement of the district's long-term strategic value.

headline: NEW FOUND GOLD RETURNS 110.47 G/T Au OVER 2.6m AT SURFACE — Iceberg Zone Grade Control Hits Bonanza Grade at Queensway, Newfoundland
snippet: New Found Gold (TSX: NFGC) reported grade control drilling results at the Iceberg zone of its Queensway project in Newfoundland returning 110.47 g/t gold over 2.60 metres and 14.58 g/t gold over 12.00 metres from surface — confirming that high-grade mineralisation at Iceberg extends to surface and intersects the anticipated mining envelope. Grade control drilling that matches or exceeds resource-model estimates is the validation event that underpins mine design confidence, and surface bonanza grades of 110 g/t are exceptionally rare in a resource-conversion campaign, suggesting Queensway's geological model may be conservative rather than optimistic.

headline: ONYX GOLD EXTENDS TREND TO 4KM WITH 24.8m AT 1.6 G/T Au AT NEW SE TARGET — Third Distinct Zone Found in 110,000m Program at Munro-Croesus, Ontario
snippet: Onyx Gold (TSX-V: ONYX) returned 24.8 metres at 1.6 g/t gold at a new target approximately 3.6 kilometres southeast of its flagship Argus North zone at the Munro-Croesus Project in northern Ontario, extending the gold-bearing trend to approximately 4 kilometres and opening a third geologically distinct target within a single property. With 110,000 metres of drilling underway and 36 holes from this batch alone, Onyx is building a systematic picture of a multi-zone gold system in the Timmins camp — a district that includes past producers and several multi-million-ounce deposits. The separate QFP porphyry intersect of 0.6 g/t Au over 69.0 metres adds a potential bulk-tonnage dimension to what has been primarily a high-grade vein story.

headline: FURY GOLD INTERCEPTS 9.81 G/T Au IN SEVEN ZONES AT EAU CLAIRE — Phase 2 Resource Conversion Advances James Bay Quebec Deposit
snippet: Fury Gold Mines (TSX: FURY) reported that hole 26EC-134 at its Eau Claire deposit in Quebec's James Bay region returned 9.81 g/t gold over 2.99 metres within seven distinct mineralised zones encountered in a single drill hole — a result consistent with the stacked, continuous nature of the deposit's mineralisation style. The Phase 2 resource conversion program is designed to reclassify inferred resources into measured and indicated categories, which is the prerequisite for a bankable feasibility study; intersecting multiple zones at grades above the deposit average in a single infill hole is a positive sign for the confidence classification of the forthcoming updated resource estimate.

headline: AUSTRAL RESOURCES DRILLS 14m AT 3.00% Cu IN FIRST ASSAYS — Enterprise Project Queensland Opens 2026 Program Above Junior Copper Average
snippet: Austral Resources (ASX: AR1) reported that the first assay batch from its 2026 drilling program at the Enterprise copper project in Queensland returned 14 metres at 3.00% copper — a grade that substantially exceeds the typical economic threshold for open-pit copper mining of around 0.5-0.8% copper. Enterprise sits in Queensland's mining corridor with established processing infrastructure and direct export access; a 3% copper opening result from the first six drill holes provides a high-grade anchor for further resource definition at a time when copper's supply fundamentals remain structurally positive despite November's AI-driven price volatility.

headline: MASSIVE METALS MERGES WITH ARGENTUM SILVER TO ADVANCE ADMIRAL BAY ZINC — C$30-40M Financing Planned for One of World's Largest Undeveloped Zinc Resources
snippet: Massive Metals and Argentum Silver (TSX-V: ASL) announced a share exchange agreement for a proposed reverse takeover of Argentum by Massive Metals, tied to a planned C$30-40 million financing, with the combined entity focused on advancing the Admiral Bay zinc-lead-silver project in Western Australia — consistently described as one of the largest undeveloped zinc resources in the world. The structure creates a vehicle with both a TSX-V listing and a substantial project footprint at a time when zinc's market is tightening; for retail investors, the Admiral Bay resource scale means any re-rating driven by development milestones would happen against an unusually large underlying asset. The deal is subject to board, shareholder and regulatory approvals.

headline: ENERGY FUELS TO PRODUCE 1M LB URANIUM AT WHITE MESA MILL STARTING DECEMBER — Only Licensed US Conventional Uranium Mill Ramps Up Ahead of Q1 2027
snippet: Energy Fuels (NYSE American: UUUU) announced on November 23 that it will launch a major uranium processing campaign at its White Mesa Mill in Utah starting December 2026, targeting approximately 1 million pounds of uranium concentrate by Q1 2027. White Mesa is the only fully licensed and operating conventional uranium mill in the United States, and a production campaign of this scale makes it the most immediate domestic supply addition for US utilities seeking non-Russian uranium under long-term contracts currently priced above $98 per pound. The campaign positions Energy Fuels directly in the path of utility procurement demand that is expected to accelerate ahead of the December FOMC meeting regardless of interest rate outcomes.

headline: CANALASKA FINDS POSSIBLE NEW BASEMENT TARGET 120m BELOW PIKE ZONE — West McArthur Summer Results In; New Athabasca Uranium Target Identified at Cameco JV
snippet: CanAlaska Uranium (TSX-V: CVV) completed its 2026 summer program at the West McArthur JV in Saskatchewan's eastern Athabasca Basin — 12,652 metres in 16 holes — reporting elevated radioactivity in hole WMA115 approximately 120 metres down-dip of the high-grade Pike Zone, which the company is interpreting as a possible new basement-hosted uranium target. The Pike Zone is one of the highest-grade uranium discoveries in the Athabasca Basin's history, with individual intersections up to 85.4% U₃O₈; the identification of a separate basement target suggests the mineralising system extends structurally beyond the known Pike Zone footprint and provides drill-ready targets for 2027 at CanAlaska's 83.35%-owned JV with Cameco.

headline: NEXGEN'S PATTERSON CORRIDOR EAST HIGH-GRADE URANIUM ZONE REACHES 739m VERTICAL — Athabasca Basin's Deep Extension Keeps Growing
snippet: NexGen Energy's (TSX/NYSE: NXG) Patterson Corridor East high-grade zone at the Rook I project in Saskatchewan now reaches 739 metres vertically, based on preliminary handheld scintillometer readings from the latest 2026 drill program — a significant structural extension that expands the zone's depth profile well beyond earlier estimates. While these are preliminary readings pending lab confirmation, the PCE zone has consistently converted handheld readings into high-grade assays in prior drill campaigns; a 739-metre vertical extent positions PCE as a resource addition target for NexGen's already-approved Rook I mine development, potentially improving the project's long-term economics beyond those reflected in the current feasibility study.

headline: COPPER PHYSICAL PREMIUM HOLDS EVEN AS PAPER PRICE BREAKS $12,000 — Supply Crunch and AI Selloff Are Pulling the Metal in Opposite Directions
snippet: Australian Mining's November analysis makes the case that copper's violent LME selloff is being driven by financial market deleveraging rather than deteriorating physical demand, pointing to Chinese buyers paying record physical premiums even as the LME breaks below $12,000 per tonne — a 17% decline from September's record. The piece argues that the disconnect between paper-market prices and physical demand is consistent with a positioning shock rather than genuine demand destruction, and that supply fundamentals — a structural mine supply deficit emerging through 2027-2028 — have not changed during the AI selloff. For retail investors evaluating junior copper positions, the analysis frames the current drawdown as a risk management challenge rather than a thesis-breaker, while acknowledging that financing conditions for junior developers tighten regardless of the physical market's underlying health.
